subject: Weekly Revision
summary: a mixed revision of the week: IC engine cycles, combustion and performance, refrigeration and air-conditioning, complex integration and numerical methods, steam and hydraulic turbines, and the iron–carbon diagram and heat treatment of steels

questions.text: Detonation (knock) in a spark-ignition engine is caused by
opts: auto-ignition of the end gas ahead of the advancing flame front
a long ignition delay of the fuel injected
pre-ignition of the charge by the spark plug before the spark occurs
incomplete combustion due to a lean mixture
questions.ans: (A) auto-ignition of the end gas ahead of the advancing flame front
solution: Concept: In an SI engine the flame travels from the spark plug across the chamber, compressing the unburnt end gas ahead of it.
If the end gas reaches its self-ignition temperature before the flame arrives, it auto-ignites almost instantaneously, producing pressure waves and the knocking sound: (A).
A long ignition delay is the cause of knock in CI (diesel) engines; pre-ignition by hot spots is a different phenomenon.
Exam tip: SI knock is reduced by high-octane fuel, retarded spark, lower compression ratio and cooler charge — the opposite of what reduces CI knock.

questions.text: In a trial on a diesel engine, fuel (calorific value 42 000 kJ/kg) is burnt at 8 kg/h, and cooling water flows at 0.2 kg/s with a temperature rise of 15 °C (c = 4.18 kJ/kg·K). The percentage of the fuel energy carried away by the cooling water (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Heat balance sheet: each item is expressed as a percentage of the fuel energy supplied.
Exam tip: A typical diesel engine heat balance: brake power 30–35 %, cooling water 25–30 %, exhaust 25–35 %, unaccounted the rest.

questions.text: An air-standard Diesel cycle (γ = 1.4) has a compression ratio of 16, and the fuel is cut off at 6 % of the stroke. Its thermal efficiency (in %, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Cut-off at k % of the stroke: V3 = Vc + k Vs, so ρ = 1 + k(r − 1).
Exam tip: Do not take ρ = 0.06 or 1.06; the cut-off percentage refers to the swept volume, not the clearance volume.

questions.text: In a lithium bromide–water vapour-absorption refrigeration system,
opts: lithium bromide is the refrigerant and water the absorbent
water is the refrigerant, so the system cannot produce temperatures below about 0 °C
ammonia is added as the refrigerant
a mechanical compressor raises the pressure of the refrigerant vapour
questions.ans: (B) water is the refrigerant, so the system cannot produce temperatures below about 0 °C
solution: Concept: In absorption systems the refrigerant is the volatile component and the absorbent takes it up in the absorber.

In LiBr–water units, water evaporates at very low pressure in the evaporator (refrigerant) and LiBr solution absorbs it; water freezes at 0 °C, so these units are used for air-conditioning (chilled water at 5–10 °C): (B).
In the NH<sub>3</sub>–water system ammonia is the refrigerant and water the absorbent, so sub-zero temperatures are possible.
Exam tip: The generator, absorber and pump replace the compressor; the input is mainly heat, not work.

questions.text: A 5 TR ammonia refrigerator (1 TR = 3.517 kW) has a refrigerant enthalpy of 100 kJ/kg at evaporator inlet and 245 kJ/kg at evaporator exit. The specific volume of the vapour at compressor suction is 0.5 m³/kg and the volumetric efficiency of the compressor is 80 %. The swept-volume rate needed (in m³/s, round off to four decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Mass flow = capacity/refrigerating effect; actual suction volume = ṁv; swept volume = actual volume/ηv.
Swept volume rate = 0.1213 × 0.5/0.8 = 0.0758 m³/s
Exam tip: Lower evaporator pressure → larger suction specific volume → a bigger compressor for the same capacity.

questions.text: A room has a sensible heat load of 25 kW and a latent heat load of 5 kW. Its room sensible heat factor (RSHF), and the effect of a rise in occupancy that adds mainly latent load, are
opts: 0.83; the RSHF rises and the supply air may be more humid
0.83; the RSHF falls and the supply air must be drier
questions.ans: (B) 0.83; the RSHF falls and the supply air must be drier
solution: Concept: RSHF = room sensible heat/(sensible + latent heat).
More latent (moisture) load makes the RSHF smaller; to absorb the extra moisture the supply air must have a lower specific humidity, and the RSHF line on the psychrometric chart becomes steeper: (B).
Exam tip: Auditoriums and kitchens (many people, cooking) have a low RSHF; computer rooms have an RSHF close to 1.

questions.text: Let C be the circle |z| = 1 traversed anticlockwise. The value of ∮<sub>C</sub> dz/(z² + 4) is
solution: Concept: Cauchy's theorem: the integral of a function analytic on and inside a closed curve is zero.
The singularities of 1/(z² + 4) are z = ±2i, both with |z| = 2 > 1, i.e. outside C.
The integrand is analytic inside C, so the integral is 0: (D).
Exam tip: Always locate the poles first; only those inside the contour contribute residues.

questions.text: The root of x = cos x (x in radians) is sought by the Newton–Raphson method starting from x<sub>0</sub> = 0.5. The value of x<sub>1</sub> (round off to four decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: x1 = x0 − f(x0)/f′(x0) with f(x) = x − cos x, f′(x) = 1 + sin x.
Exam tip: Keep the calculator in radian mode for trigonometric equations.

questions.text: The integral of x⁴ from x = 0 to x = 3 is evaluated by Simpson's 3/8 rule with three equal strips (h = 1). The value obtained (round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Simpson's 3/8 rule: I = (3h/8)[f0 + 3f1 + 3f2 + f3]; it is exact for cubics only.
Exam tip: Simpson's 3/8 rule needs the number of strips to be a multiple of 3; the 1/3 rule needs an even number.

questions.text: The hydraulic turbine whose runner blades can be rotated about their own axes while the turbine is running, giving a high efficiency at part load, is the
solution: Concept: Part-load efficiency depends on how well the blade angles match the changed velocity triangles.
In a Kaplan turbine both the guide vanes and the runner blades are adjustable (double regulation), so the efficiency curve is flat: (C).
A fixed-blade propeller turbine has a sharply peaked efficiency curve; a Francis turbine adjusts only its guide (wicket) gates.
Exam tip: Kaplan turbines suit low heads (about 2–70 m) with large, variable flows, e.g. run-of-river plants.

questions.text: The isentropic enthalpy drop in the nozzle of an impulse steam turbine is 180 kJ/kg and the nozzle efficiency is 92 %. Neglecting the velocity of approach, the steam velocity at nozzle exit (in m/s, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Steady-flow energy equation for an adiabatic nozzle: V2 = √(2 ηn Δhs), with Δh in J/kg.
Actual drop = 0.92 × 180 = 165.6 kJ/kg
Exam tip: The shortcut V = 44.72√Δh (Δh in kJ/kg) gives the same result.

questions.text: For a given head and power, choosing a turbine of higher specific speed means that
opts: the turbine runs faster, so the turbine and generator are smaller and cheaper
the turbine runs slower and needs a larger generator
the turbine must be of the Pelton type
the risk of cavitation is reduced
questions.ans: (A) the turbine runs faster, so the turbine and generator are smaller and cheaper
solution: Concept: Ns = N√P/H5/4; for fixed P and H, N is proportional to Ns.
A higher speed means a smaller runner and a smaller, cheaper generator (fewer poles): (A).
But high-specific-speed (Kaplan) runners have high relative velocities and low pressures at exit, so they are more prone to cavitation and need a lower setting.
Exam tip: Thoma's critical cavitation factor rises steeply with specific speed.

questions.text: The engineering stress–strain curve of mild steel is shown with points A to E. The lower yield point is
solution: Concept: Mild steel shows a sharp yield point: the stress drops from the upper yield point and then fluctuates about a lower value while Lüders bands spread.
A = proportional limit, B = upper yield point, C = lower yield point, D = ultimate tensile stress, E = fracture (engineering stress falls after necking).
The lower yield point C is taken as the yield strength in design: (D).
Exam tip: The yield-point phenomenon is caused by carbon and nitrogen atoms pinning dislocations (Cottrell atmospheres).

questions.text: A plain carbon steel with 1.0 % C is slowly cooled to room temperature. With the eutectoid at 0.76 % C and cementite at 6.67 % C, the mass percentage of pearlite in its microstructure (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: A hypereutectoid steel consists of pearlite plus proeutectoid cementite (at the grain boundaries); use the lever rule just below 727 °C.
Pearlite = 95.94 %, proeutectoid cementite = 4.06 %
Exam tip: The grain-boundary cementite network makes slowly cooled hypereutectoid steels brittle; they are spheroidised before use.

questions.text: The amount of retained austenite in a hardened high-carbon steel can be reduced by
opts: quenching from a higher austenitising temperature
solution: Concept: As carbon and alloy content rise, Mf falls below room temperature, so some austenite remains untransformed after quenching.
Cooling the steel to −80 °C or below (sub-zero treatment) takes it past Mf and converts most of the remaining austenite into martensite: (C).
A higher austenitising temperature dissolves more carbon and Ni/Mn lower Ms, both increasing retained austenite.
Exam tip: Gauges and bearings get sub-zero treatment for dimensional stability.
